says: L23 says a resend of a start answer adds nothing, but fabsh's start_child_err (program.ts:204, `() => true`) settles whichever start waits oldest, so the same refusal folded twice fails a second start; L23's walk tries a refusal's resend only when no other start waits, which leaves out exactly this case.
proof: A scratch script on the library's stepper: two starts ('counter as a1', 'counter as b2'), then one forbidden answer gives [failed a1, starting b2], and the same answer folded again gives [failed a1, failed b2]. start.laws.test.ts:415 reads 'a resend is tried only when no other start waits'. Today the mailbox writes a resend under the same id as one line (processes/Mailbox.ts, 'the resend is one line'), so a real run does not fold it twice.
cost: The law claims more than the code holds. If an answer is ever folded twice, a start shows the wrong failure and its own answer never lands.
